newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun Q1 helped by U.S. performance. [CORRECTED 07:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun Q1 helped by U.S. performance. [CORRECTED 07:25 GMT]

text.p: British composite insurer Royal & Sun Alliance Group Plc reported a 24 percent rise in first quarter profits on Tuesday, helped by a rebound in results from North America.
Pre-tax operating profits for the first three months of the year rose to 195 million pounds ($320.6 million), up from 157 million pounds in 1996.
Royal Sun said the fiugures represented an encouraging start to the year with a strong performance in North America, a broadly unchanged result in the UK and a rise in life profits.

The integration of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance Insurance following last year's six billion pound merger was continuing in line with the timetable to achieve at least the forecast annual cost savings of 175 million pounds, it said.
(Corrects value of merger from six million).

Together with the approval from shareholders at the annual meeting to buy back up to five percent of the group's shares, the performance confirmed the commitment to deliver shareholder value, it added.
A 34 million pound fall in weather-related costs contributed to a 42 million pound increase in U.S. general business to 51 million pounds.
In contrast, a 10 million pound rise in UK subsidence costs more than accounted for the five million pound drop in UK general business profits to 50 million pounds.
